classifications.complementary: Different jobs that combine well in one workflow.
classifications.recommended alternative: Pick one; the choice depends on the brief.
classifications.optional: Adds value only for specific briefs.
classifications.redundant: Same job; using both adds cost without benefit.
classifications.potentially conflicting: Both try to own the same asset, timeline, hook or rule set.

evidence_levels.tested: Run by a fixture in this catalogue; see the named fixture.
evidence_levels.documented: Stated in the pinned upstream documentation; not run here.
evidence_levels.proposed: A file handoff this catalogue suggests; not documented upstream and not run here.

roles.guidance: Skills and lists that shape decisions.
roles.execution: Libraries, models and apps that produce artifacts.
roles.orchestration: Systems that run other tools in order.
roles.storage: Memory, graphs and logs that keep project knowledge.

pairs.note: Choose one design authority. Meng To skills are scoped recipes; load one for a specific effect rather than as the authority.
One critic per pass. Impeccable's detector can still run in CI while Hallmark owns a review.
Both supply animated React components. React Bits is MIT plus Commons Clause: the components may ship inside a product but may not be resold.
One prototype owner. Stitch is hosted; Penpot can be self-hosted; Open Design is a local-first agent workspace.
Designlang extracts tokens from a site; Awesome DESIGN.md is a set of example files. Both describe real brands: use them for principles on your own or permitted sites, never to copy a brand.
Both install PreToolUse hooks that can block Read. Run at most one, or prefer a plain decision log. Claude Mem sends analytics by default.
One generator per asset. SF3D needs about 6 GB VRAM; TRELLIS.2 at least 24 GB; SAM 3D Objects at least 32 GB plus a mask.
MeshAnything V2 caps output at 1,600 faces and its code license is non-commercial. Deformation topology for characters still needs Blender retopology.
UniRig predicts skeleton and skin; Blender corrects them. Blender rigging and weight validation were tested in fixtures/blender-glb; UniRig was not run.
Dream Textures generates or projects color images; Blender nodes assemble the full PBR set and color spaces.
Blender Skills can drive Blender headless or through an optional Blender MCP server.
Dream Loop routes image-to-3D through fal.ai and its Plus workflow says not to model in Blender. Choose one loop owner.
ComfyUI-3D-Pack runs SF3D, TRELLIS v1, Hunyuan3D, TripoSG and 3DGS nodes natively. SAM 3D Objects, TRELLIS.2, UniRig and MeshAnything V2 run standalone with file handoffs.
Different representations for different deliverables. A Gaussian PLY is not a polygon mesh; conversion is lossy and unverified here.
One timeline authority. HyperFrames documents a Remotion port skill.
Both edit the cut. Interchange of editable timelines is unverified.
fixtures/blender-glb: Blender 5.2.2 GLB with skin and clip loaded by three r187; scale, up axis, skin, clip and seek checks passed.
fixtures/seekable-scene: DevTools frame capture of a seekable Three.js scene encoded by FFmpeg 7.1; seekable, repeatable, pause-to-play and stream checks passed.
Open Design documents a native HyperFrames workspace.
Video Use generates animation overlays with HyperFrames or Remotion.
ComfyUI-3D-Pack documents a native Stable Fast 3D node.
UniRig writes its merged results through Blender's Python module (bpy 4.2).
A spec from Spec Kit could be indexed by Graphify. Spec Kit init was tested; the combination was not.
Each turns a topic or product into a finished film with its own timeline. Pick one per film.
kit/framecap pauses gsap.globalTimeline and seeks it per frame: within 0.054 px in its test.
HyperFrames lists GSAP among its animation runtimes.
ComfyUI hosts the 3D node pack. Give the pack its own install.
Agent skills for Remotion projects.
EffectCraft is an app-style compositor; HyperFrames and Remotion are code-first. One timeline authority.
One runtime per game. Godot for editor-driven 2D/3D games and native exports, Phaser for small web-first 2D, Bevy for Rust/ECS teams, Babylon.js for full 3D games in the browser.
Both render glTF in the browser. Three.js (with React Three Fiber) for bespoke scenes, Babylon.js when the brief needs a game engine's physics, audio, input and inspector.
Godot 4.4 added Jolt as a 3D engine option and projects created from 4.6 default to it. Use the built-in module; a standalone Jolt build is only for custom C++ engines.

One physics solver per world. Rapier for Rust/Bevy or WASM, Jolt for C++ and Godot 3D, Matter.js for 2D browser games. fixtures/game-dev steps Matter.js and Rapier at a fixed 1/60 s and checks repeat runs match.
Phaser bundles a modified Matter.js 0.20. Use the bundled copy; adding a second Matter.js package gives two engines that disagree.
bevy_rapier lives in the Rapier repository and must match the Bevy version (0.37 targets Bevy 0.20 at the pinned commits).
Godot MCP launches the editor, runs projects with full script execution and reads console output. It cannot see the running scene tree; check gameplay yourself.

Colyseus for room-based authoritative state in Node.js; Nakama for a full backend (accounts, storage, matchmaking, leaderboards, chat). fixtures/game-dev runs a Colyseus room on loopback; Nakama was not run.
Pixelorama for sprites and tiles, Blockbench for blocky low-poly models, Blender for everything else. Export PNG sheets or glTF and validate them in the engine.
LDtk exports JSON levels; each engine needs a loader or adapter. Validate layers, collisions and entities after import.
jsfxr generates short retro effects as WAV; Howler.js plays them in the browser behind a user gesture. jsfxr's WAV output is tested in fixtures/game-dev; Howler.js playback was not run.

Ink compiles branching stories to JSON; inkjs runs them in a web game. The pinned ink README lists no Godot integration. fixtures/game-dev tests inkjs compile, branches and save/load on their own, not inside Phaser.
@theatre/r3f requires @react-three/fiber ^8 (React 18), but R3F at the pinned commit is v9 (React 19). Drive R3F from Theatre's core sequence yourself, or pin R3F 8.
Both write the same CSS properties. Give each property one owner; fixtures/expressive-motion shows a deliberate conflict where the last writer wins.
One clock per scene. GSAP for timelines, Motion for React UI and gestures, Theatre.js for keyframes edited in a studio panel. All three seek in fixtures/expressive-motion.
React Three Fiber is a React renderer for Three.js, not a second engine. Match React, Three.js and R3F versions; use frameloop="demand" or "never" for seekable renders.
motionmaxxing's runtime builds on GSAP and vendors Three.js. Keep whichever compositor already owns the timeline.
reanimate compares a recapture against an authorized motion reference; a design critic reviews the result. Do not promise exact replication.
Both add punchy effects. pixelfx for pixel-art games and sprite sheets, Sakuga VFX for anime-style web interaction bursts.
